_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS R1256's CONTRACT IS NOT VACUOUS — run it from the
WHAT THE CONTRACT IS. A tracked injection sweep's `test_command` is a cargo
command this repository issues, and until this round it was in no law's
population — the fifth such place, after the workflows, the shell, the
workspace lister and the build-machine declaration. Twenty-six of the
thirty-three were resolving freely when the population first opened.
WHY IT MATTERS MORE FOR A SWEEP THAN ANYWHERE ELSE. A sweep edits the tree,
runs, and restores exactly the files it edited. A cargo command without
`--locked` that meets a disagreeing lockfile REWRITES it — and that file is
not one the harness edited, so it is not one the harness puts back. The run
reports the tree returned to what it was, and leaves a change behind.
THIS MANIFEST IS ITSELF IN THE POPULATION IT IS ABOUT, which is the shape
this repository keeps arriving at and keeps wanting: the law reads the file

injections.name: the-fifth-source-is-dropped-from-the-population
injections.why: the state every sweep was in until this round, and the one that reads as compliance: a law that looks at less finds less, and a population with a source missing has no way to say so. The per-source floor is what turns the absence into a red rather than a smaller clean number

injections.name: a-sweep-resolves-freely-again
injections.why: the defect this round FOUND, in one file rather than twenty-six. `.githooks/injection-sweep.json` runs the hook suite against an edited tree; without `--locked` a disagreeing lockfile is rewritten by the run and left behind by the restore

injections.name: a-sweeps-suite-is-read-as-one-nothing-judges
injections.why: the other law over the same population, and the reason a second judge had to be NAMED rather than assumed. A sweep's suite has no wrapper in front of it because the harness IS the wrapper — it holds each run's target set against the control's. Take that sentence out and twenty-six suites read as unjudged, which is a true-looking finding about a population that is judged twice over

injections.name: a-listing-is-read-as-a-test-run
injections.why: R1266 — `cargo test … -- --list` prints the names a harness knows and RUNS NOTHING, so there is no coverage for the wrapper to hold a log against; read as a run it is a true-looking finding about a command that never had the property. It arrived here the moment R1266 made `item-citations`' assembled argv readable, and the law was right to refuse a command it could not place — what was missing was the population, not the wrapper

injections.name: a-build-without-a-run-is-read-as-a-test-run
injections.why: `--no-run` builds the test binaries and runs none of them, which is the other half of the same fact; the reading is here rather than in the law because it is a fact about the command, and `unrun-tests` assembles exactly this shape
